character_sheet: Jeffery is the Giant Robot under another name: a subclass with the same stat block — 550 HP, 40 attack, 18 armour (MobStats.JEFFERY, Jeffery.java:26-33; the class comment calls it a named-skin alias, :11-16) — on the same rig: a hip bar under three stacked back blocks, a shoulder bar, a neck and a head, one thigh (three pieces) and one shin with a three-piece foot, and one arm of three pieces with knuckles — eighteen classic parts, the leg and the arm each drawn TWICE, once per side, at mirrored offsets (ModelGiantRobot.createBodyLayer, ModelGiantRobot.java:75-169; renderToBuffer :241-262) — so the rig carries twenty-nine bones: the seven unshared parts and one bone per side for each of the eleven shared leg and arm parts (`thigh__i0` the left thigh, `thigh__i1` the right, and so on: the converter's render_instances expansion, the final bone set). It inherits everything the Giant Robot does (GiantRobot.java): wanders far, walks through villages and looks about (:70-89), and on a 1-in-5 tick takes its target — anything living and not a monster or a creative player within 16 blocks (:248-265) — aims its head within 0.5 rad and fires a laser ball from a muzzle 3.75 blocks ahead and 10 up (fireLaserBall :192-216) and, within eight blocks plus half the target's width, raises the attacking flag and punches (customServerAiStep :139-181, doHurtTarget :120-132). Cactus cannot hurt it and a mob attacker becomes its target (hurt :238-246). It spawns under the Giant Robot's rules (checkSpawnRules :286-294); no biome file names `jeffery` in the port's data today. Read it as the Giant Robot: the hips sway and bob, the legs swing stiffly, the arms windmill when it fights.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig by the Giant Robot's renderer (GiantRobotRenderer.java:25, applied :37; shadow 0.99) on a 256x512 sheet (ModelGiantRobot.java:169); 3.0 x 9.75 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:102-104; the design's row writes [4,10]). The geo is the reference leg's converter output over the port's compiled model with the render_instances form (owner 2026-09-14, item 2): the shared thigh, shin, foot and arm parts, drawn twice per frame at mirrored offsets (ModelGiantRobot.java:247-253), are one bone per draw — `<part>__i0` the sign +1 pass (the model's left side: +x, vanilla's left_arm side) and `<part>__i1` the sign -1 pass (the right). The bind pose is the constructor pose: the hip bar along z, the two legs at z +13 / -13 (the hip's constant quarter turn is setupAnim's, :208, and carries them to x +13 / -13 in-game), the arms at x +26 / -26, the forearms pitched -0.196 rad. The design's row said 'G1 must create distinct left/right bones before any profile can exist': these are them, the FINAL bone set.

groups.name: gait
groups.axis: x (the thighs, shins and hip pitch), y (the hip yaw), with the hip's bob
groups.amplitude: x a move scale of 0.65 x the walking speed capped at 1: the hip pitches pi x 0.1 = 0.314 rad (18 deg) on a cosine and yaws the same on a sine about pi/2, and bobs 4 units at twice the stride; the thighs pitch pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg) about −0.196 x the scale, the two legs half a period apart and a quarter ahead of the hip; the shins pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) about +0.628 x the scale, half a period apart; the feet take the shin angle; the whole torso rides the bob
groups.plain: the hips sway and bob with the walk while the two legs swing stiffly half a period apart, thigh and shin on their own phases, and the torso and head ride the bob
groups.math: ms = min(1, amount * 0.65); hip.xRot = cos(-t * 0.25) * pi * 0.1 * ms; hip.yRot = pi/2 + sin(-t * 0.25) * pi * 0.1 * ms; hip.y = -60 + 4 cos(-t * 0.5) ms; thighAngle0 = cos(-t * 0.25 + pi/2) * pi * 0.15 * ms - 0.196 ms; thighAngle1 = cos(-t * 0.25 + 3pi/2) * ... - 0.196 ms; shinAngle0 = cos(-t * 0.25 + pi) * pi * 0.2 * ms + 0.628 ms; shinAngle1 = cos(-t * 0.25) * ... + 0.628 ms; the left leg (sign +1: thigh__i0, thigh2__i0, thigh3__i0 at thighAngle0 and shin__i0, foot1/2/3__i0 at shinAngle0), the right leg (sign −1: the __i1 bones at thighAngle1 / shinAngle1), each thigh placed 13 units from the hip by the hip's angles and the shin 40 units down the thigh; back1/2/3, shoulders, neck, head .y = hip.y
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is −ageInTicks x WING_SPEED 0.25 (a negative phase: the cosine is even, the sine odd): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.25 = 25.1 ticks; the bob runs at twice that rate (12.6 ticks)

groups.name: arms
groups.axis: x (the arm swing), y (the shoulders' twist)
groups.amplitude: not attacking: each arm takes the OTHER leg's thigh angle (arm A the second leg's, arm B the first's) — the walk's swing at the stride's 0.25 rad/tick — and the shoulders yaw against the hip's sway; attacking: a windmill punch at 0.5 rad/tick — the upper arm pi/5 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) about −pi/4 + 0.628, the forearm the negative plus pi + 0.628, arm B on the opposite sine — and the shoulders twist pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) on the same sine
groups.plain: the arms swing with the walk, opposite their legs, and windmill in wide punches with the shoulders twisting while the attacking flag is set
groups.math: calm: armA1 = armA2 = thighAngle1, armB1 = armB2 = thighAngle0, shoulders.yRot = -hipYAngle; attacking: armA1 = sin(t * 0.5) * pi/5 - pi/4 + 0.628, armA2 = -(sin(t * 0.5) * pi/5 - pi/4) + pi + 0.628, armB1 = -sin(t * 0.5) * pi/5 - pi/4 + 0.628, armB2 = -(armB1 - 0.628) + pi + 0.628, shoulders.yRot = -sin(t * 0.5) * pi * 0.2; back3.yRot = shoulders.yRot / 2; the left arm (sign +1: arm1__i0 / arm2__i0 at armA1, arm3__i0 / knuckles__i0 at armA2 - 0.196), the right arm (sign −1: the __i1 bones at armB1 / armB2), each 26 units out from the hip
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (GiantRobot.java:49, set at :168 within eight blocks plus half the target's width, cleared at :171 / :176 / :179) selects the windmill
groups.omega_note: the classic phase attacking is ageInTicks x WING_SPEED 0.25 x 2 = 0.5 rad/tick (period 12.6 ticks); calm, the arms follow the stride's 0.25

behaviour: The rig is twenty-nine bones drawing a two-legged, two-armed robot from eighteen classic parts: the thigh (three pieces), shin and foot (three pieces) are drawn twice per frame, once per leg with that leg's angles and mirrored hip offsets, and so are the three arm pieces and the knuckles (ModelGiantRobot.java:241-262, renderLeg :269-300, renderArm :307-317) — the converter's render_instances form gives each draw its own bone (`<part>__i0` the left side, `<part>__i1` the right; owner 2026-09-14, item 2), the distinct left and right bones the design's row requires, and the FINAL bone set; the hook animates each side's bones with that side's angles when the rig lands.

The walk is scaled by 0.65 x the walking speed capped at 1 (:187-190): the hip pitches and yaws 18 degrees on a 0.25 rad/tick wave (a 25-tick period) and bobs 4 units at twice that rate (:193-194, :205-208); the thighs swing 27 degrees a quarter turn ahead of the hip and the shins 36 degrees, the two legs half a period apart (:195-202); the whole torso, neck and head ride the bob (:232-235) and the head turns the look yaw and a third of the pitch (:236-237).

Not attacking, each arm swings with the other leg's thigh angle and the shoulders yaw against the hip's sway; while the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte is set (GiantRobot.java:49, raised at :168 within eight blocks plus half the target's width) the arms windmill 36 degrees at 0.5 rad/tick in punches and the shoulders twist 36 degrees with them, the upper back block half as much (:210-229).

The laser (fireLaserBall, GiantRobot.java:192-216) and the punch (doHurtTarget :120-132) are rolled by customServerAiStep (:139-181), inherited unchanged by Jeffery (Jeffery.java:17) — nothing in the code fires an animation for them.

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelGiantRobot row (geckolib_migration_design.md:447): 'head [2.5,2] @1; shoulders [4,1.8] @0.5; hip [3,2] @0.5; each replayed thigh/shin segment [1.2,3] @0.5; each arm chain [1,2.5] @0.5; feet/knuckles [1.6,1.2] @0.25' — 'Its legacy model replays shared parts at two transforms; G1 must create distinct left/right bones before any profile can exist.' head, shoulders and hip resolve as written. The distinct left / right bones exist now (owner 2026-09-14, item 2: the converter's render_instances expansion, the FINAL bone set): 'each replayed thigh/shin segment' is thigh, thigh2, thigh3 and shin PER SIDE — thigh__i0 / thigh__i1 and so on (__i0 the sign +1 pass, the model's left side at +x; __i1 the sign -1 pass, the right; the port's renderToBuffer comment words the +1 pass as 'right arm' from the viewer's side — the labels follow the model's own convention, vanilla's left_arm at +x); 'each arm chain' is arm1, arm2, arm3 per side; 'feet/knuckles' is foot1, foot2, foot3 and knuckles per side — 25 entries, every one in the geo. The same list as `giant_robot`'s: 'Separate equal-size profiles'.
formulas: The Giant Robot rig's formula through the shared hook (`JefferyGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations` -> `GiantRobotGeoReplacement.poseRig`; Jeffery extends GiantRobot, a port-side registry drawn by the one GiantRobotRenderer with its texture, shadow and scale): `ModelGiantRobot.poseFrom`, `renderLeg` and `renderArm` (ModelGiantRobot.java:193-246, :277-308 and :315-331 - the pose statements of the two leg and two arm passes that renderToBuffer :249-275 draws; orig ModelGiantRobot.java:169-278 in `render` (func_78088_a, :150-279, the leg passes inline at :173-199 and :200-226 and the arm passes at :243-254 and :255-266; func_78087_a at :287-289 is a bare super call), wingspeed 0.25 from `new ModelGiantRobot(0.25f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:516 - the port's WING_SPEED): the move scale is the walking speed times 0.65 clamped to 1. The hip pitches by the cosine of minus the age in ticks times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.1, times the move scale, yaws a quarter turn plus the sine of the same, times pi, times 0.1, times the move scale, and sits at -60 plus 4 times the cosine of minus the age times the wingspeed times 2, times the move scale; the three back pieces, the shoulders, the neck and the head take the hip's height. The two thigh angles are the cosine of minus the age times the wingspeed plus a quarter turn (the first) and plus three quarter turns (the second), times pi, times 0.15, times the move scale, less 0.19634954 times the move scale; the two shin angles the cosine of minus the age times the wingspeed plus a half turn (the first) and unshifted (the second), times pi, times 0.2, times the move scale, plus 0.62831854 times the move scale. Not attacking, the shoulders yaw by minus the hip's sway and the arm angles copy the thigh angles crosswise; attacking, the shoulders yaw by minus the sine of the age times the wingspeed times 2, times pi, times 0.2, and the arms windmill: the upper angle is the sine of the age times the wingspeed times 2, times pi over 5, less a quarter turn, the lower angle a half turn minus it, both plus 0.62831853, the second arm on the negated sine; the third back piece yaws by half the shoulders' yaw. The head yaws by the look yaw in radians and pitches by a third of the look pitch in radians. Each leg pass (the sign +1 for the first, -1 for the second) puts the thigh's three pieces at the hip's place plus the sign times 13 units along the hip's pitch and yaw (x by the cosine of the pitch times the sine of the yaw, y by minus the sine of the pitch, z by the cosine of the pitch times the cosine of the yaw), pitched by that pass's thigh angle; the shin and the three foot pieces pitch by the shin angle and sit 40 units down the thigh's pitch. Each arm pass puts the two upper arm pieces 60 above the hip, the sign times 26 to the side and the sign times minus 26 times the sine of the shoulders' yaw back, pitched by the upper angle; the forearm and the knuckles pitch by the lower angle less 0.19634954 and sit 41 units down the upper arm's pitch. The walk position plays no part; the port draws each shared leg and arm part twice per frame (the rig's <part>__i0 / __i1 clones). The GeckoLib hook is the same (JefferyGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
